Monday: Our student team presented a model of a parcel locker for an apartment building. We had spent hours making the screen bright and the symbols attractive. During a demonstration, a resident praised the display, then set her shopping bags on the floor before opening a door. We assumed the door needed a stronger motor. She explained that she had put down her bags because she could not tell where to pull.
Wednesday: We replaced the working screen with a printed sheet and built several cardboard door handles. This rough model let us change parts between tests instead of waiting for new electronic components. We asked residents to collect a parcel while carrying their usual belongings. A handle that seemed obvious to us disappeared from view behind a full shopping bag. A colored arrow helped people find it, but the narrow grip remained difficult to hold.
Friday: We enlarged the grip and moved it away from the door's edge. Residents could now spot it and pull without first emptying their hands. The caretaker asked whether we were ready to install the final version. I wanted to say yes, especially after all the work we had done. Instead, we arranged another test with delivery workers, whose gloves might create different difficulties. Our first assumption had sent us toward a stronger motor; watching someone use the locker had sent us toward a different handle. I no longer wanted to treat a successful demonstration as the end of the investigation.
q: Which statement best describes how the diary develops?
choices: A series of tests confirms the first motor theory.
Repeated observations lead to a revised design.
An attractive display solves a problem with doors.
An improved model removes the need for more tests.

Welcome to Keeping It Working. In this room, you will find two portable music players. Both still play songs clearly. One has a cracked cover; the other has a battery that no longer holds much charge. Their owners stopped using them, although most of their parts still work. Beside each player is a card showing the price of the device when new and the price quoted for a repair. We have left the purchase dates covered for now.
Listen to the repair shop recording before lifting the cards. A worker explains that the cracked cover can be replaced with basic tools. The second player presents a different problem. Its battery was made especially for that model and is no longer sold. The repair would require finding a used battery, with no guarantee of how long it would last. A low purchase price may therefore hide a barrier to keeping a device in use. Now lift the cards. The player that is harder to repair was bought more recently.
Our exhibition does not suggest that every broken object deserves a costly repair. Instead, it asks you to look beyond an item's age and its first price. The repair estimates show what different owners would need to spend to keep listening to music. At the exit, compare the two estimates and consider what else you would want to know before deciding whether to repair or replace a device.
q: Which title best captures the exhibition's central concern?

How New Models Reduce the Cost of Repairs
Why Owners Stop Listening to Portable Players
The Changing Appearance of Music Players

An undo button makes a screen feel forgiving. Delete the wrong sentence, restore it, and nothing seems lost. That experience can encourage us to experiment. Its secretary accidentally removes Friday's rehearsal, and the system immediately sends a cancellation message to every member.
The secretary notices the mistake and presses undo. Friday's rehearsal appears on the calendar again. Yet one member has already accepted a work shift, and another has arranged to meet a friend. The screen has returned to its earlier state; their plans have not. A correction message helps, but it cannot ensure that everyone will read it before making other arrangements. Restoring a record and restoring the situation it created are different tasks.
Should the club therefore remove the undo button? That would make correction harder without preventing the original error. A better approach would let the secretary preview schedule changes before releasing them to members. The system could also make clear when a change has already produced a public message. People should not have to guess whether they are revising a private draft or taking an action others will respond to.

Monday, April 6. My drawing notebook now has a calendar inside its cover. Every evening I sketch one object on the kitchen table, then color a square. At first, the growing line of squares pleased me more than the drawings. I kept checking how many days I had managed without a break. If I missed an evening, I planned to draw twice as long the next day to make up for it.
Thursday, April 16. A weekend visit to my cousins left two empty squares. Back home, I looked at the broken line and put the notebook away. The next evening, I wanted to sketch a spoon, but starting again seemed pointless: my longest run was already ruined. Three more evenings passed before I noticed that the calendar, which was meant to help me draw, had become a reason to avoid drawing.
Tuesday, April 21. Yesterday I drew the spoon for five minutes. I left the empty squares as they were and added a small arrow beside the new sketch. The arrow means I came back. I will still record my evenings, but I want to notice returns as well as long runs. My drawings have not suddenly become better. Yet tonight I opened the notebook without calculating how much work I owed it.

Dear Advice Desk: Whenever my friend complains about her weekend job, I offer a plan. I have suggested changing shifts, speaking to her manager, and finding another job. She rejects each idea and recently said I was not listening. But I remember every problem she mentions. How can she say that? Signed, Puzzled.
Dear Puzzled: Remembering the facts is one part of listening. Finding out what the speaker needs is another. Your friend may be trying to describe a difficult day before she decides whether anything needs to change. An immediate plan can leave that part of the conversation unfinished. She may feel dismissed even when you have correctly understood the events.
Next time, briefly reflect what you heard: "It sounds as though you felt left out when the schedule changed." Then check whether that is accurate. You might also ask, "Would you like ideas, or would it help to talk this through?" Neither question requires you to agree that her manager behaved badly. You are checking your understanding, not judging a person you have never met.
Your suggestions may become useful later. If she asks for them, offer one and explore it together rather than handing her a complete list. She may also want a different response on a different day. Treat her answer as guidance for this conversation, not as a permanent rule about your friendship.
q: What is the primary aim of this reply?
choices: To evaluate the fairness of a work schedule.
To help a reader respond to a troubled friend.
To recommend a way to select weekend jobs.
To explain how managers can prevent complaints.
explain: 回覆說明如何確認朋友當下需要的支持，目的是改善回應方式。「評估班表公平」只是來信背景，回覆者沒有判定主管對錯。

Every Friday, Eli left the school radio room while I was still working. As the final song played, I filed the requests and put away the spare cables. He returned just as I switched off the equipment. In the empty corridor, he could hear problems that passing students might otherwise cover with their voices.

I had filled that short word with an entire story about him. Before the next broadcast, I asked him to add his checking route to the sheet. Then I wrote down the tasks each of us did out of the other's sight.

A Duty Sheet Leaves Part of the Story Untold

At Rillstone Quarry, the main attraction is an absence: a vast space where a hill once stood. The former stone works has no restored village or rows of souvenir shops. Instead, visitors follow the cut walls to see the marks left by different tools. In the afternoon, low sunlight makes those marks easier to see. A small shelter near the entrance explains how to recognize them, so it is worth stopping there before you walk.
Two routes explore the quarry. The lower path is broad and level, with benches placed along it. The upper route climbs a steep stairway to a ledge. Visitors can take this route only with a local guide on weekend mornings, stopping at places from which workers once lowered stone. The views from the ledge are wider, but the marks in the walls can be studied just as well from below.
Allow for a full afternoon if you choose the lower path and want time to sketch or read the shelter's notes. Food is not sold inside, though drinking water is available at the entrance. Visitors seeking an exciting climbing challenge may find the pace slow. For those who enjoy noticing small details, however, the quarry turns an ordinary walk into a quiet lesson in how people have changed the land.

Nora Chen spent years as a badminton singles player, measuring a good match by the points she won. When her club asked her to try doubles, she brought the same habit with her. She chased shots her partner was ready to return and left open spaces behind her. During practice, the coach counted a rally as successful only when both players had covered their assigned areas. Gradually, Nora learned that leaving a shot to someone else could be the better decision.
Across town, stage designer Leo Wu faced a similar problem. His early sets were full of bright color and moving parts. Audiences remembered the scenery but sometimes missed the actor standing in front of it. Leo began watching rehearsals from the back row. In one production, he removed a large painted screen, making a small movement by the lead actor stand out. The scene gained force as the set grew simpler.
Neither Nora nor Leo has given up personal skill. Nora still practices difficult shots, and Leo still puts new visual ideas to the test. But both now keep some of their ability in reserve, using it when the shared task calls for it. Their experience suggests that a contribution should be judged by what it makes possible for others, as well as by how much attention it wins for its maker.
q: How are the first two paragraphs related?
choices: They trace two stages in one person's career.
They present similar lessons in different fields.
They compare two approaches to sports coaching.
They contrast a player's aims with a designer's.

subject: english
passage:
A mountain covered in winter snow may seem far removed from a farmer's summer worries. Yet, in regions with dry summers, the connection is close. Much of the year's rain and snow arrives when fields need little water. __1__ This delay helps keep streams flowing after the wet season has ended and crops have begun to grow.
A warmer winter can change that schedule. More water may fall as rain, or the snow may melt earlier, sending water downhill sooner. __2__ A river running high in March may therefore offer little comfort to a farmer facing dry fields in August. Even a year with a familiar total of rain and snow can bring unfamiliar difficulties.
Measuring the frozen supply presents another challenge. Two snow layers of equal depth can contain different amounts of water because one may be loose while the other is tightly packed. __3__ Workers therefore collect samples and measure the water they contain. A photograph of a white mountain cannot provide the same information, however impressive the snow looks.
Water managers combine these sample results with records of when streams rise and fall. __4__ The samples answer the first question; the stream records answer the second. Together, the answers can guide decisions about storing water for later use. Snow is thus more than a white covering: it connects one season's weather with another season's needs.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？

More water in spring means more is available in late summer.
Some winter water stays frozen instead of flowing downhill.

subject: english
passage:
Host: Welcome to Coast Radio. A listener asks why seawater sometimes turns colder after several windy days, even in summer. Is the wind simply cooling it? Scientist: That is not the whole explanation. Under suitable conditions, wind moves surface water away from the coast. __1__ This replacement is called upwelling, and it connects the sunny surface with deeper water.
Host: Does this movement matter to ocean life? Scientist: Yes, and temperature is only part of the story. __2__ In sunlight, tiny floating plants can use these materials to grow. Without a fresh supply, growth near the surface may slow, even when there is plenty of light. The wind can therefore influence the amount of food available.
Host: But fish cannot eat the wind. How does the extra plant growth help them? Scientist: We need to follow the feeding sequence. __3__ Small fish then eat those animals, and larger fish may eat the smaller fish. Through these links, a change in the water can eventually affect animals much bigger than the plants that first responded.
Host: So should fishers expect a larger catch as soon as the water turns cold? Scientist: Not necessarily. Think about all the growth and feeding just described. __4__ This delay means that a visitor arriving just after upwelling starts may find few extra fish. Also, the winds can change. A cold reading is a useful clue about conditions, but it is not a promise of fish waiting below the boat.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Even after the upward flow begins, its effects on fish numbers need time to develop.
Colder water rises from below to take the place of the water that has moved away.
The first step involves small animals eating the newly grown plants.
These sheltered pools also protect young fish from the force of breaking waves.
Beyond its cooling effect, this upward flow supplies nutrients that support plant growth.
explain: 前文表層水離岸，後文 this replacement（這項替換）須指下方冷水補位。「supplies nutrients」中的 this upward flow 尚無前文指涉對象。

subject: english
passage:
At a nature center in eastern North America, I tried to draw the journey of monarch butterflies. I gave one orange butterfly a name and drew its path from Mexico to Canada and back. A guide watched me complete the circle. __1__ She suggested that I follow a family instead, and we began again with the spring journey.
Butterflies that have spent winter in Mexico start flying north when spring arrives. They lay eggs on milkweed plants, whose leaves provide food for the young. These adults die before the population has spread all the way north. __2__ Some of these new travelers also produce young along the route. The arrows on my page now connected several lifetimes, each covering part of the distance.
I assumed the southward journey would work in the same way. __3__ These butterflies can survive far longer than the summer generations. They delay breeding, travel south to Mexico, and remain there through winter. Many live long enough to begin moving north the following spring. The journey south is therefore possible within a single lifetime, unlike the entire northward journey to Canada.
Back at the table, I kept the circle but erased the butterfly's name. I used different colors for successive generations on the northward section and one color for the southward section. __4__ That change made the drawing less like a holiday route and more like a record of lives connected across seasons. I had needed more than arrows to understand what was traveling.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Their offspring continue the journey north in their place.
These wing tags helped us identify the returning insects.
The line now traced a family, not one butterfly's travels.
In late summer, however, a longer-lived generation appears.
The guide asked if one butterfly could fly the whole circle.
explain: 前文把整圈畫成一隻蝶的旅程，後文卻改追蹤家族，故接導覽員質疑能否飛完整圈。最後修圖才以線條表達家族，此處尚未修改。

subject: english
passage:
Welcome to the woodland spring walk. Along this path, small wildflowers appear before many visitors expect the growing season to begin. For the best view, stop beside the first bend and look both down and up. __1__ Light passes between their bare branches and reaches the flowers below. The ground is warmer than in winter, yet still unusually bright for a forest.
These early flowers are often called spring ephemerals because their visible season is brief. They quickly produce leaves, open flowers, and make seeds while sunlight remains available. __2__ By then, the wildflowers' own leaves may be turning yellow. Their disappearance is connected to the changing cover above them, rather than to a failure to take advantage of spring.
If you return in midsummer, you may see few traces of the same plants. However, a bare patch does not mean that they have died. Their underground parts remain alive after the shoots disappear. __3__ That stored supply supports them through the months without leaves and helps power their rapid growth the following spring. Please leave the soil undisturbed as you pass.
At the final bend, find the numbered wooden marker beside the path. Take a photograph that includes both the forest floor and the branches above it. __4__ The pair of images will let you compare the open spring view with the summer shade. Seen together, they show how a small plant can use a brief opportunity beneath much taller neighbors, without growing tall itself.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Their opportunity closes as the trees spread a roof of new leaves overhead.
Return to this marker in summer and take another photograph from the same position.
For these few weeks, the trees have yet to open the leaves that will shade the ground.
Those wind-carried seeds will let the flowers begin growing in a more distant forest.
The living parts below the surface save food made during the bright weeks of spring.
explain: 後文 their bare branches（它們的光禿枝條）需要先引入尚未長葉的樹木，並銜接向上看的提示。「new leaves overhead」已是成葉遮蔭階段，與後文相反。

Dear residents of Ash Lane: Our street in Britain has many green gardens, but hedgehogs may experience it as a series of walls. These small animals search for food at night and can cover a surprising distance between feeding places. __1__ A rich garden behind a solid fence may offer them less than a modest garden with an accessible entrance.
I propose that willing neighbors connect their back gardens with small openings through the fences. Before any work begins, we should mark the proposed openings on a simple plan of the street. __2__ Without that second opening, a garden enclosed on every other side becomes a dead end. We need to consider the next boundary as well as our own.
Some residents worry that joining gardens will also let their pets wander away. __3__ An opening of this size lets a hedgehog pass, but some small pets could also fit through it. Owners must check their own animals before agreeing. Shared boundaries require agreement from both sides, and nobody should alter a neighbor's fence without discussing the plan first.

subject: english
passage:
Ask someone what sits inside a wooden pencil, and the answer may be "lead." The familiar name points to a mistake in the object's early history. In sixteenth-century England, people found a dark material that left clear marks on ordinary white paper. __1__ We now call that material graphite, and it is a form of carbon.
Early pencil makers cut this material into sticks and wrapped them in string or fitted them into wooden holders. They depended on pieces suitable for cutting. __2__ This powder-based approach was used by Nicolas-Jacques Conte in France. He mixed graphite with clay, shaped the mixture into thin rods, and heated them. Each pencil no longer required one perfect piece of natural graphite.
__3__ Of these two benefits, the second depended on the balance of the two ingredients. More clay made a point harder and its marks lighter. More graphite produced a softer point and darker marks. A factory could therefore use the same basic materials to serve different needs. Drawing deep shadows and making fine lines did not require an identical tool.
In a shop, a pencil's outside may tell you little about the darkness of its marks. Two pencils with the same yellow paint can behave very differently. __4__ In this code, H refers to hardness, while B refers to blackness. These marks help buyers choose a tool for neat notes or dark shadows without testing every pencil.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Makers later learned to turn powder into writing sticks.
A letter code indicates the marks this recipe produces.
This metal coating also kept the user's fingers clean.
Its appearance led people to mistake it for lead.
The recipe eased production and let makers vary the marks.
explain: 前文指出名稱源於誤認，後文才正名為 graphite（石墨），故填因外觀相似而誤認為鉛。metal coating（金屬鍍層）找不到前文依據。

subject: english
passage:
Dear Hana, The white walls and pointed roofs of Alberobello in southern Italy looked like a scene from a storybook. Our guide called these stone buildings trulli. At first, I assumed they had been designed mainly to be admired. __1__ Some sheltered farm workers, while others provided space for storing crops and tools. Their unusual appearance had distracted me from these ordinary purposes.
The materials also connected the buildings to daily work. Fields around the town contained plenty of limestone, and farmers removed loose stones while preparing the ground for crops. __2__ Builders could use what was nearby instead of bringing every piece from far away. Clearing a field and finding material for shelter were thus related activities.
I then asked how the pointed roofs stayed up. The guide described a method that used carefully placed stones without cement to hold them together. __3__ The opening therefore becomes smaller toward the top until a final stone can close it. The shape I had treated as a playful decoration followed from the arrangement of the material.
Near the end of our walk, we passed a trullo with washing hanging outside. The farm shelters, field stones, and roof design now seemed connected to the family living there. __4__ For that reason, I stayed in the street rather than walking through the open door for a closer look. I will show you photographs of the roof, but the family's kitchen is not in my album. Love, Emma.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Each higher ring of roof stones extends farther inward.
This mixture had to dry before the next ring was added.
Their early uses, however, served everyday farming needs.
Seeing trulli as homes meant respecting their residents.
These stones turned a farming problem into a resource.
explain: 前句只看建築外觀，後句列出農工住所及儲藏用途，故填 early uses（早期用途）作轉折。在地石材句談材料，無法引出用途列舉。

subject: english
passage:
Interviewer: Why does an old canal need a path beside it when boats travel on water? Historian: __1__ Before engines were common, a horse walked along this strip of land, pulling a loaded boat with a long rope. The water carried the weight while the animal supplied the forward pull. One worker guided the horse while another steered the boat. The route on the bank and the route in the water worked together.
Interviewer: Did the rope leave evidence? Historian: __2__ Years of rubbing cut grooves into stone at certain bridge corners. A visitor may mistake them for damage caused by weather, but their position reflects the line taken by the towing rope. The stone recorded many ordinary journeys without recording the names of the boat crews.
Interviewer: Could horses follow the canal through every tunnel? Historian: No. Some early tunnels had no path beside the water. __3__ Lying on the boat, workers pressed their feet against the tunnel walls to push it onward. Meanwhile, someone led the horse over the hill to the other end. Boat and horse took separate routes, meeting again beyond the dark passage.
Interviewer: What should a visitor look for during a canal walk? Historian: Notice the path, the rope marks, and the tunnels. __4__ The last of these jobs can be hard to imagine beside a quiet canal in daylight. Looking at these details helps us picture the effort once required to deliver a load.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Ropes rubbing against bridge corners left lasting marks.
These clues suggest leading horses, steering, and pushing.
That path once carried the animals that pulled the boats.
In such tunnels, human legs took over from the horses.
Deeper channels let larger loads pass under the bridges.
explain: 題目問岸邊道路的用途，後文用馬拉船說明，故填供動物帶動船隻的陸路。In such tunnels（在這類隧道內）限定隧道情境，無法解釋此處的道路。

subject: english
passage:
A German child's first school photograph may include a large paper cone. Called a Schultüte, it is filled with treats, little gifts, or useful classroom supplies. The custom goes back to the nineteenth century. __1__ In other words, it celebrates a beginning rather than rewarding results.
A cone can be bought or made at home. To a child, a favorite animal drawn on plain paper may matter more than a costly decoration. __2__ The first depends on knowing a child's interests; the second can be read from a price tag. The two should not be treated as the same achievement.
__3__ Those extra centimeters can make the cone harder for a small child to carry. More sweets do not automatically make the classroom less unfamiliar, either. When adults compete over size, the original purpose can slip from view. The child still faces a new room, teacher, and classmates.
A modest cone can still do its job. For example, a familiar snack can give a child something easy to talk about with a new classmate. A ruler or a little notebook can be useful on the first morning. __4__ This question shifts attention from what other parents will admire to what the child will actually experience.
Keeping an old custom does not require every family to fill the same container in the same way. It requires a clear sense of why the gesture matters. If we remember the nervous beginner at the center of the photograph, we are more likely to fill the cone with care.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: How can gifts ease fears and suit a child's interests?
Children get this gift before their first school lesson.
A larger cone does not guarantee a more confident child.
How can these gifts be stored safely until term's end?
Personal meaning and market value are separate measures.
explain: In other words（換言之）重述入學禮在首次上課前收到，慶祝開始而非獎勵成果。term's end（學期末）問的是存放時間，不能導出這項重述。

subject: english

Dear Leo, you asked why our washing machine was silent when you visited on Saturday morning. Dad had recently joined the night team at a warehouse. I first thought he was spending his mornings in bed to avoid family chores. __1__ That reversal meant that eight in the morning was his time to settle down, not to go out.
Keeping the house quiet took some planning. The kitchen shares a wall with his bedroom, and the machine shakes during its final cycle. __2__ My sister could still prepare a cold breakfast, while I waited until the evening to wash clothes. That arrangement reduced the noise without requiring us to leave the house or sit still all morning.
For a while, we thought the problem was solved. __3__ Relatives assumed that being home meant being available, so they asked him to collect parcels or attend afternoon meetings. We began telling them which hours he had set aside for sleeping. His rest needed space in the family calendar, just like our classes and their office hours.
Now, we leave a short note on the table about the day's plans. Dad reads it after waking and joins us for an early dinner before work. __4__ He helps with homework then, and we hear about his shift. I no longer judge his contribution by whether he is awake when I happen to need something.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Yet silence alone could not protect the time he needed for sleep.
This difference in pay was enough to persuade Dad to keep the night job.
That meal has become our regular time to catch up with one another.
His working day was ending just as the rest of ours began.
We therefore moved the loudest chores to the hours when he was away.
explain: 夜班結束正逢家人白天開始，形成 That reversal（那種顛倒）所指的作息對比，並解釋八點就寢。「挪動家務時段」談家務安排，未交代父親與家人相反的作息。

For a month, striped socks seemed to be everywhere at Larch High. They appeared beside classroom doors, on the stairs, and in photographs shared after lunch. Some teachers described the sudden fashion as another example of students copying one another without thinking. __1__ They had been asked to wear the stripes so a director could quickly find them during rehearsals in a crowded hall.
By the week of the performance, friends outside the cast had started wearing similar pairs. They bought tickets, helped paint scenery, and wanted a visible way to encourage the actors. __2__ The same pattern on the same item had acquired a new message. Someone looking only at their feet would have missed the difference between a performer and a supporter.
A photograph from the final show made the trend appear even bigger. It showed a row of students in striped socks near the stage, while the many plain socks farther back were outside the frame. __3__ Some students later said they had felt unusual for not joining, until they looked around their own classrooms and noticed how many others had also stayed with ordinary pairs.
After the show, the stripes gradually disappeared. One actor stopped wearing them because the rehearsals were over; a supporter simply found the thick socks uncomfortable as the weather grew warmer. __4__ Describing the change as everyone rejecting yesterday's fashion would hide both stories. An item can become common for several reasons, and lose its popularity in just as many ways.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: The photograph made a small, highly visible group look like the whole school.
At first, though, the matching socks identified members of a theater cast.
Even the disappearance of the stripes did not have one shared meaning.
These sales figures allowed the shop to order the most popular size in advance.
For these later wearers, the socks signaled support rather than a part in the play.
explain: though（不過）轉折「盲目模仿」的評語，指出起初是劇組識別；後句 They 指演員。「後來穿的人」尚未出現，且聲援者不必供導演在排練時辨識。

Welcome to your first morning at our storm relief donation center. The piles beside the door may make it tempting to send a truck immediately. However, moving a large quantity of goods is not the same as meeting a need. __1__ This list names blankets and soap as today's priorities; toys are not currently requested, even though several bags have arrived.

A worker at the other end should not have to open six mixed packages to find one blanket. __2__ Those details allow the receiving team to place goods where they belong without unpacking everything first. Keep the writing visible when you stack the finished boxes.
__3__ Such a change might occur if another town delivers enough blankets before our truck leaves. In that case, the receiving staff might ask us to send more soap instead. Check with the coordinator before loading, and be ready to revise the contents and labels together. A neatly packed box is not a reason to ignore information that has just arrived.
At the end of your shift, you may want to judge the morning by how many boxes you carried. That number describes your effort, but it leaves out the final step. __4__ Their confirmation allows the coordinator to close each request. A photograph of a loaded truck cannot tell us this. q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？

Write the contents and the number of items clearly on the outside of each box.
This delivery route lets our drivers stop at every damaged house before sunset.
First, compare the donations with the latest list sent by the receiving centers.

subject: english
q: The ____ for bicycle parking exceeds what the station can provide; all spaces fill before seven each morning.
explain: demand 是「需求」。車位每天很早就滿，表示需求超過供給。capacity 是「容量」，指車站可容納的車數，與人們需要多少車位不同。

subject: english
q: After the suitcase fell from the truck, we checked it for ____; the broken handle meant it would need repairs.
explain: damage 是「損壞」；摔落後把手斷裂，必須修理。moisture 是「濕氣、水分」，不能解釋把手斷掉。

subject: english
q: Nora could not ____ on the instructions with a game going on outside, so she found a quieter room.
explain: concentrate on 是「專心於」；外面吵鬧，所以換安靜處。comment on 是「評論」，題目強調噪音妨礙專注，並非發表意見。

subject: english
q: The dancer lost her ____ when the stage tilted, but she caught a railing and remained on her feet.
explain: balance 是「平衡」；舞臺傾斜，她抓欄杆才沒跌倒。rhythm 是「節奏」，失去節奏不必靠欄杆站穩。

subject: english
q: One ____ of sharing an office is lower rent, although finding a quiet place for private calls can be difficult.
explain: benefit 是「好處」；分租能降低租金，後半句另提缺點。requirement 是「必要條件」，低租金是分享辦公室的好處而非先決條件。

subject: english
q: A whistle announced the train's ____; it rolled out of the station as a late passenger rushed onto the platform.
explain: departure 是「出發、離站」；列車駛出車站，遲到者來不及上車。arrival 是「抵達」，與 rolled out「駛出」相反。

subject: english
q: The friendly conversation came to a surprisingly ____ end when the caller hung up in the middle of a sentence.
explain: abrupt 是「突然的」；話說一半就掛斷，結束得出乎意料。gradual 是「逐漸的」，不符合突然中斷。

subject: english
q: The research reports used to require a paid account. They are now ____ to everyone through the library's free website.
explain: accessible 是「可取得、可使用的」；報告由付費改為免費開放。familiar 是「熟悉的」，開放閱讀不代表每個人都熟悉內容。

subject: english
q: The note was ____: 'next Friday' meant this week to some staff and the following week to others.
explain: ambiguous 是「有歧義的」；未標日期，員工產生兩種解讀。accurate 是「準確的」，不能說明同一句話造成不同日期的理解。

subject: english
q: There was ____ seating in the hall; several rows stayed empty even after the largest group arrived.
explain: ample 是「充足的」；最大團體進場後仍有數排空位。scarce 是「稀少、不足的」，與仍有大量空位的線索相反。

subject: english
q: The map was sold as an ancient document, but its paper was made last year. Clearly, it was not ____.
explain: authentic 是「真實的、非偽造的」；去年才製成的紙不可能是古文件的原件。accurate 是「準確的」，紙張年代無法判定地圖內容是否正確。

subject: english
q: To reduce ____ in judging, paintings were shown without names so judges could not favor their own students.
explain: bias 是「偏見、偏袒」。隱去姓名是為防止評審偏愛自己的學生。confusion 是「困惑、混淆」，與對特定參賽者偏心不同。

subject: english
q: Once cheated by a seller, Ian was ____ about online bargains and checked each seller's record before ordering.
explain: cautious 是「謹慎的」；曾受騙，因此下單前查賣家紀錄。optimistic 是「樂觀的」，不能表達因受騙而加強查證的態度。

subject: english
q: Open windows improve air ____ in the classroom, allowing fresh air to enter while warm, stale air moves outside.
explain: circulation 是「循環、流通」；新鮮空氣進入、污濁空氣排出。density 是「密度」，不是空氣進出的流動過程。

subject: english
q: To ____ the confusing assignment, the teacher gave a specific example of what she meant by 'a personal response'.
explain: clarify 是「澄清、說明清楚」。老師用具體例子幫助學生理解作業要求。postpone 是「延後」，涉及時間安排，不能表達以例子消除疑惑的目的。

subject: english
q: Deep cracks in the old bridge's supports could cause it to ____ under a crowd's weight, so engineers closed it.
explain: collapse 是「倒塌」。支柱有深裂縫，承受人群重量時可能崩塌。strengthen 是「變堅固、增強」，與支柱受損而有承重危險的情況相反。

subject: english
q: The camera's ____ design lets it fit in a pocket, yet it has all the controls found on our much larger model.
explain: compact 是「小巧、緊湊的」；功能相同卻能放進口袋。complex 是「複雜的」，不代表體積小，勿因控制功能多而誤選。

subject: english
q: Despite his qualifications, the translator was not ____ enough for the job; even simple sentences contained errors.
explain: competent 是「稱職、有能力的」；連簡單句子都有錯，顯示能力不足。confident 是「有自信的」，出錯不代表缺乏自信，不能由此推定。

subject: english
q: Even after a long workday, the ____ technician checks every measurement twice and completes all the safety records before leaving.
explain: diligent 是「勤勉、認真的」。忙了一整天仍複查測量、完成紀錄，顯示做事用心。conscious 是「有意識、清醒的」，無法表達持續認真工作的態度。

subject: english
q: The water ____ campaign urges hotels to fix leaks and reuse laundry water, reducing the amount drawn from wells.
explain: conservation 是「節約、保育」；修漏水、回收用水都是節水。consumption 是「消耗、用量」，不是保護與節省資源的行動。

subject: english
q: The proposal remained ____ after months of public debate; residents were still sharply divided over the new road.
explain: controversial 是「有爭議的」；公開討論數月仍意見分歧。confidential 是「機密的」，與 public debate「公開辯論」不符。

subject: english
q: Rejecting ____ staging, the director had the audience walk among the actors instead of watching from fixed seats.
explain: conventional 是「傳統、慣常的」；觀眾離開固定座位，在演員間走動，打破慣例。experimental 是「實驗性的」，新演法正屬嘗試新形式。

subject: english
q: Her words were polite, but the anger in her voice still helped ____ feelings she was trying to hide.
explain: convey 是「傳達」。措辭雖客氣，憤怒的語氣仍傳達了她想隱藏的感受。conceal 是「隱藏」，與語氣讓人察覺感受的結果相反。

subject: english
q: The town plans to ____ the old station, keeping its outer walls but turning the waiting room into a market.
explain: convert 是「改建、改變用途」。保留車站外牆，將候車室改作市場。destroy 是「摧毀」，與保留建築結構並重新使用的計畫相反。

subject: english
q: The clerk admitted that the false entries were ____, explaining that he had changed the numbers to hide missing money.
explain: deliberate 是「故意的」；改數字是為了掩飾款項短少。accidental 是「意外的」，與明確的掩飾目的矛盾。

subject: english
q: The two farms share a stone wall that marks their ____; each family is responsible for the land on its own side.
explain: boundary 是「邊界」；石牆兩側的土地分屬兩家。entrance 是「入口」，不是區分土地歸屬的界線。

subject: english
q: Local residents ____ the plan to build a factory near their homes because they fear more noise and air pollution.
explain: oppose 是「反對」：居民擔心工廠帶來噪音與空氣污染，所以反對興建。approve「批准」與擔憂相反；announce「宣布」、postpone「延後」是主事者才能做的決定，也不是擔憂的反應。

subject: english
q: The writer makes no ____ between fact and opinion, presenting her own guesses as if they were confirmed information.
explain: distinction 是「區別」，make a distinction between 指區分兩者；把猜測當事實，表示未區分。connection 是「關聯」，不是分辨差異。

subject: english
q: The separate fees seem small, but they ____ a large sum when combined, leaving me little money for other expenses.
explain: add up to 是「合計為」；個別費用雖少，加總卻很高。result from 是「起因於」，把各項費用與合計金額的關係說成因果。

subject: english
q: After agreeing to share the rent for a year, Paul tried to ____ the agreement when he found a cheaper room elsewhere.
explain: back out of 是「退出、不履行」；先同意分租，找到便宜房間後想反悔。go ahead with 是「照計畫進行」，與反悔方向相反。

subject: english
q: The distant job pays more, but ____ the travel costs before deciding whether you would have more money left.
explain: bear in mind 是「記住、考慮到」；薪水較高仍須扣除交通費。keep pace with 是「跟上」，此處要納入成本考量，不是追趕。

subject: english
q: Seeking freedom to make decisions, members voted to ____ the national association and form an independent club.
explain: break away from 是「脫離」；為自主決策而另組獨立社團。get along with 是「與……相處融洽」，不包含退出原組織。

subject: english
q: Rescuers decided to ____ the search after the missing hikers returned and reported that everyone was safe.
explain: call off 是「取消、停止」；失蹤者全員平安，已不需搜尋。step up 是「加強」，與人已找到的情境相反。

subject: english
q: After missing a week of school, Joy spent the weekend trying to ____ her lessons so she could follow Monday's class.
explain: catch up on 是「補上落後的進度」；缺課一週後須補課業。cut down on 是「減少」，會更難跟上週一課程。

subject: english
q: While searching a drawer for batteries, I was surprised to ____ my grandfather's missing letter beneath a stack of maps.
explain: come across 是「偶然發現」；找電池時意外找到祖父遺失的信。send for 是「派人取來、寄信索取」，屬主動索取而非碰巧找到。

subject: english
q: The company kept calling us with excuses for late deliveries. After three missed deadlines, we could no longer ____ it.
explain: count on 是「依靠、指望」。公司仍持續來電，但三度逾期，失去的是對履約的信任。hear from 是「收到……消息」，與持續來電的線索不符。

subject: english
q: The storm ____ communication with the island; for two days, families had no way to contact relatives there.
explain: cut off 是「切斷、中斷」；家屬兩天無法聯絡島上親人。brought back 是「恢復、帶回」，與通信中斷的結果相反。

subject: english
q: To reduce waste, the cafe plans to ____ disposable cups and serve every drink in a washable mug instead.
explain: do away with 是「廢除、去除」；改用可清洗杯來減少垃圾。put up with 是「忍受」，並未表示停止使用免洗杯。

subject: english
q: With no manual available, the crew had to ____ knowledge gained on earlier trips to repair the unfamiliar engine.
explain: draw on 是「運用、憑藉」；無手冊，只能用過往經驗修理。make up 是「編造」，此處知識來自先前旅程，並非憑空捏造。

subject: english
q: The receptionist can ____ guests' complaints and arrange repairs, although she has no power to change room prices.
explain: deal with 是「處理」；接待員可受理抱怨並安排修理。approve of 是「贊同」，贊同抱怨不等於處理問題。

subject: english
q: Our roof repair estimate did not ____ the labor needed to remove old tiles, so the final bill exceeded our budget.
explain: allow for 是「把……考慮在內」；低估費用是因漏算拆瓦工資。amount to 是「合計為」，後接總額，不能表達預估漏列成本。

subject: english
q: The museum shipped the equipment at its own ____, so our club paid nothing for delivery or insurance.
explain: expense 是「費用」，at one's own expense 指自費。社團不用付運費或保險費，表示由館方負擔。risk 是「風險」，承擔風險與負擔費用不同。

subject: english
q: The policy aims to be ____, giving all applicants the same chance regardless of income or personal connections.
explain: fair 是「公平的」；不論收入或人脈，每位申請人機會相同。strict 是「嚴格的」，著重要求嚴，不表示機會平等。

subject: english
q: Despite repeated requests to change the deadline, the teacher remained ____ and accepted no work submitted after Friday.
explain: firm 是「堅定的、不讓步的」；拒收週五後的作業，顯示立場不變。flexible 是「有彈性的」，與不接受延期相反。

subject: english
q: Staff are trained to ____ complaints calmly, even when customers shout at them or demand immediate refunds.
explain: handle 是「處理」；櫃檯人員須冷靜處理顧客抱怨。submit 是「提交」，submit complaints 是提出申訴，與此處服務人員的角色不符。

subject: english
q: For her loan application, Mei listed her wages and the rent paid by her tenant as monthly ____.
explain: income 是「收入」，工資及收到的房租皆屬收入。profit 是「利潤」，指收入扣除成本後的餘額，不能直接等同這兩筆所得。

subject: english
q: His recovery was ____: each week he could walk farther, until he finally regained full strength.
explain: gradual 是「逐漸的」，每週走得更遠呈現漸進過程。partial 是「部分的」，只描述恢復程度，未表達每週逐步進展。

subject: english
q: Visitors waited at the museum's ____ while a guard checked their tickets before allowing them inside.
explain: entrance 是「入口」；驗票後才獲准進入，表示遊客在入口等待。exit 是「出口」，方向與 allowing them inside 不符。

subject: english
q: Although the street names had changed, the route seemed ____ to Mei; she remembered every turn from her childhood walks.
explain: familiar 是「熟悉的」；雖路名改變，仍記得兒時走過的每個轉彎。complex 是「複雜的」，不是此處記得路線的重點。

subject: english
q: With the door closed, the smoke left only a ____ smell that most people in the hallway failed to notice.
explain: faint 是「微弱的」；門關著，多數人未察覺煙味，顯示氣味很淡。stale 是「不新鮮的」，描述品質，無法解釋未被察覺的強度線索。

subject: english
q: The host asked guests not to ____ the speaker; questions would be taken after the talk, when everyone could speak.
explain: interrupt 是「打斷」；問題留到報告後提出，避免打斷講者。introduce 是「介紹」，不是要求延後提問的原因。

subject: english
q: The train passengers agreed to ____ seats: he wanted her window view, while she preferred his place near the door.
explain: exchange 是「交換」；兩人各想坐對方的位置，因此互換座位。adjust 是「調整」，調整座椅角度等不會把兩人的位置對調。

subject: english
q: The app can ____ phone use during homework, locking the screen after thirty minutes even if a game is still running.
explain: limit 是「限制」；三十分鐘後鎖住螢幕，即使遊戲還在進行也不能繼續。monitor 是「監測」，僅觀察使用情形，不表示強制停止。

subject: english
q: The caller's ____ remained unknown because he used a false name and refused to say who he was.
explain: identity 是「身分」；假名與拒絕說明自己是誰，讓人無法確認身分。location 是「位置」，回答的是在哪裡。

subject: english
q: The guide's ____ told us to stop; he raised his palm without speaking so we would not disturb the nesting birds.
explain: gesture 是「手勢」；舉起手掌而未說話，仍能傳達停下的訊息。whisper 是「低聲說話」，雖小聲仍屬說話，與 without speaking 不符。

subject: english
q: The shorter workweek gives employees more ____ for hobbies and family visits without reducing their pay.
explain: leisure 是「閒暇時間」；工時縮短，便有更多時間從事嗜好及探親。security 是「保障、安全」，並非可用來安排活動的時間。

subject: english
q: Researchers will ____ duplicate names from the list, leaving one entry per person to avoid contacting anyone twice.
explain: eliminate 是「刪除、排除」；每人只留一筆資料，須刪除重複姓名。identify 是「辨認」，只找出重複資料仍未刪除。

subject: english
q: Before shipping the glass bowls, workers added padding to ____ that the pieces would remain apart during the trip.
explain: ensure 是「確保」；加緩衝材料的目的是讓碗運送時保持分開。assume 是「假定」，不能藉由假定來保護物品。

subject: english
q: Trapped without heating, the climbers had to ____ bitter cold for three nights before rescuers reached them.
explain: endure 是「忍受、熬過」；受困且沒有暖氣，三夜後才獲救，表示實際承受酷寒。avoid 是「避開」，與持續受困於低溫的情況不符。

subject: english
q: The newspaper will ____ the official's dishonesty by printing records that contradict his claims about missing funds.
explain: expose 是「揭露」；刊出與官員說法矛盾的紀錄，可揭穿謊言。dismiss 是「不予理會、駁斥」，與公開證據的目的不符。

subject: english
q: Parents on changing shifts need ____ childcare arrangements that can be adjusted whenever their work hours change.
explain: flexible 是「有彈性的」；工作時段改變時，托育安排也須能調整。rigid 是「僵化、不變通的」，與 can be adjusted 相反。

subject: english
q: Experts judged the painting ____ after matching its materials and brushwork to the artist's documented works.
explain: genuine 是「真正的」，此處指真跡，材料與筆法的比對提供真偽線索。imaginary 是「想像中的、虛構的」，與畫作實際可供檢驗的材料和筆觸不合。

subject: english
q: Engineers expressed ____ concerns after finding deep cracks in the bridge supports and urged its immediate closure.
explain: grave 是「嚴重的」；支柱深裂且建議立即封橋，表示憂慮重大。minor 是「輕微的」，與封橋處置所反映的迫切危險不符。

subject: english
q: The manager never announced the store's closure, but canceling every future order seemed to ____ it.
explain: imply 是「暗示、意味著」；雖未宣布關店，取消所有未來訂單卻暗示此事。deny 是「否認」，與取消訂單傳達的方向相反。

subject: english
q: For the first time, the town will ____ a tax on empty houses, requiring their owners to pay an extra charge each year.
explain: impose 是「課徵、施加」；首次要求屋主每年多繳費，表示開徵稅款。abolish 是「廢除」，會取消而非新增負擔。

subject: english
q: His brief reply was hard to ____: we could not tell whether he was accepting the invitation or merely being polite.
explain: interpret 是「解讀」；已收到回覆，卻無法判斷其用意。predict 是「預測」，用於尚未發生的事；translate 是「翻譯」。

subject: english
q: To prevent the illness from spreading, staff will ____ the sick animals, keeping them apart from the healthy ones.
explain: isolate 是「隔離」；讓病獸與健康動物分開，以免傳染。treat 是「治療」，並不表示分開安置。

subject: english
q: After months of testing, the firm will ____ its delivery service on Monday, when customers can first use it.
explain: launch 是「推出、啟用」；顧客首次能使用，表示服務正式上線。restore 是「恢復」，須原本已有服務而後中斷。

subject: english
q: A booking gives a photographer ____ use of the studio. Even other members must wait outside during the reserved hour.
explain: exclusive 是「專屬的」。預約時連其他會員都不能入內，表示該時段由一人專用。equal 是「平等的」，不能表達排除其他使用者的限制。

subject: english
q: This repair demands technical ____. Even with proper tools, only a trained mechanic can complete it safely.
explain: expertise 是「專業知識與技能」。有適當工具仍需受訓技師，重點是技術能力。authority 是「權限、權威」，題幹未涉及核准權限。

subject: english
q: After working through two nights, the driver showed signs of ____: his eyelids grew heavy, and he fought sleep.
explain: fatigue 是「疲勞」；連續熬夜、眼皮沉重且難以清醒都是疲累線索。boredom 是「無聊」，題幹指出的是睡眠不足。

subject: english
q: The audit uncovered ____. Staff had submitted false bills to obtain payment for services they had never provided.
explain: fraud 是「詐欺」。以虛假帳單騙取未提供服務的款項，涉及蓄意欺騙。waste 是「浪費」，不一定涉及捏造帳單騙款。

subject: english
q: The proposal drew a ____ response: angry residents shouted down its supporters and refused to discuss any details.
explain: hostile 是「充滿敵意的」；居民怒斥支持者且拒談細節，表現出強烈敵意。cautious 是「謹慎的」，並不表示主動以憤怒言行對抗。

subject: english
q: The species is now ____: its last surviving bird died in captivity, and no wild populations remain.
explain: extinct 是「滅絕的」；物種最後存活的鳥已死，野外也沒有族群，表示全數消失。rare 是「稀少的」，仍有存活個體，與線索不符。

subject: english
q: The added safety gear doubled costs, so the engineer had to ____ the expense by explaining how it prevents injuries.
explain: justify 是「證明合理」；工程師用預防傷害的效益說明額外費用值得。calculate 是「計算」，此處是在說明理由，而非算金額。

subject: english
q: The outdated computer system became a ____ when frequent crashes delayed orders and drove customers to competitors.
explain: liability 此處是「負擔、不利因素」；故障使訂單延誤、顧客流失。resource 是「資源」，強調可供運用的助益，與後果不符。

subject: english
q: Though it had no resale value, the old map proved ____ to the rescue, as it showed the only safe route to the trapped hikers.
explain: essential 是「必不可少的」。舊圖雖無轉售價值，卻標出通往受困者的唯一安全路線。trivial 是「微不足道的」，與救援必須依賴這條路線的情況相反。

subject: english
q: A shortage of translators could ____ the talks by forcing delegates to pause whenever they could not understand one another.
explain: disrupt 是「擾亂、使中斷」。缺乏翻譯迫使代表因溝通不良而暫停討論。coordinate 是「協調」，有助於活動順利進行，與談判受阻的情況不合。

subject: english
q: When her flour supplier closed, the baker had to ____ an emergency stock she had stored for such a situation.
explain: fall back on 是「轉而依靠備用資源」；供應中斷，改用預存麵粉。make room for 是「騰出空間給」，存貨早已備妥，非正在安排空間。

subject: english
q: Ben thought he had ____ copying the report until his teacher found the stolen text and gave him a failing grade.
explain: get away with 是「做壞事而未受罰」；抄襲被發現且不及格，無法逃過處罰。get around to 是「終於抽空做」，不涉及是否受罰。

subject: english
q: I spent all evening reading the manual but never ____ it; several chapters were still unread when training began.
explain: get through 此處是「讀完、完成」；仍有數章未讀，表示未能讀完。get over 是「克服、從疾病或打擊恢復」，不是完成閱讀。

subject: english
q: After weeks of resistance, the firm agreed to ____ the workers' demands and granted every requested pay increase.
explain: give in to 是「向……讓步」；從抗拒轉為同意全部加薪。come up with 是「想出、提出」，要求是員工提出，公司是接受的一方。

subject: english
q: Lena refused to ____ her promise, so she stayed late to finish the repair despite missing her bus.
explain: go back on 是「違背」；她拒絕違背承諾，寧可錯過公車也完成維修。make good on 是「履行」，若接在 refused to 後會與後續守諾的行動相反。

subject: english
q: The twins have ____ their coats; the sleeves now end above their wrists, although the fabric is still perfect.
explain: grow out of 衣物指「長大而穿不下」；袖長不足但布料完好。wear out 是「穿壞」；take in 是「改窄」，不表示長高而袖長不足。

subject: english
q: Please ____ your visitor badge at the front desk before leaving; the guards need to collect every badge issued today.
explain: hand in 是「繳回、交出」；離開前警衛要收回訪客證。hand out 是「分發」，與 collect「收回」的方向相反。

subject: english
q: The firm will ____ technical details until launch, fearing that rivals might copy the design before sales begin.
explain: hold back 是「暫不公開、扣住」；避免抄襲，等產品可售才公開細節。give out 是「發布、分發」，會使競爭者提早得知資訊。

subject: english
q: The two clubs managed to ____ their disagreements over costs by agreeing on a payment plan that satisfied both sides.
explain: iron out 是「解決、消除」；雙方接受付款方案，表示費用分歧已解決。point out 是「指出」，指出分歧不等於透過協議消除分歧。

subject: english
q: Researchers numbered each turtle to ____ its movements, recording when and where it appeared all summer.
explain: keep track of 是「持續追蹤、掌握」；編號並記錄出現時間地點，是追蹤活動。take charge of 是「負責管理」，不是持續記錄動向。

subject: english
q: With robots handling most assembly work, the factory will ____ workers despite the union's demands to protect jobs.
explain: lay off 是「解僱、資遣」；機器接手組裝，工會又要求保住工作，顯示廠方打算裁員。take on 是「雇用」，與工作被取代及工會抗議的方向不符。

subject: english
q: Maya had promised to bring the costumes, so forgetting them would ____ the performers waiting to go on stage.
explain: let down 是「使失望」。表演者等著穿戲服上台，忘記帶會讓他們失望。look after 是「照顧」，與忘帶必需用品的後果相反。

subject: english
q: The school will ____ the complaints by interviewing students and checking records before deciding if rules were broken.
explain: look into 是「調查」；訪談與查紀錄，是判斷是否違規前的調查。draw up 是「草擬」，此處申訴已存在，並非重新起草。

subject: english
q: To ____ a steady speed on the steep hill, the driver pressed harder on the gas as the road rose.
explain: maintain 是「維持」；上坡時加踩油門是為了保持穩定車速。reduce 是「降低」，與此目的相反。

subject: english
q: Eva gave a ____ response to failure: she calmly accepted blame and suggested improvements instead of accusing others.
explain: mature 是「成熟的」；冷靜承擔過失並提出改善建議，是成熟的反應。bitter 是「憤恨的」，不合冷靜負責的態度。

subject: english
q: The message changed the ____ of the room; worried faces relaxed, and laughter soon replaced the tense silence.
explain: mood 是「心情、氣氛」；擔憂的表情放鬆、笑聲取代沉默，指室內氣氛改變。structure 是「結構」，與情緒無關。

subject: english
q: The passage became so ____ near the exit that we had to turn sideways to squeeze through.
explain: narrow 是「狹窄的」；必須側身擠過，表示寬度不足。steep 是「陡峭的」，不能解釋側身的需要。

subject: english
q: Despite wanting to see the rare bird up close, visitors must ____ the rule requiring them to stay on the marked path.
explain: obey 是「遵守」；雖想靠近鳥，遊客仍須留在步道上。revise 是「修訂」，不是遊客面對此規則應有的行為。

subject: english
q: Against the white wall, the old yellow curtain looked so ____ that its color was barely noticeable.
explain: pale 是「淡的、蒼白的」；黃色幾乎看不出來，表示顏色很淡。vivid 是「鮮豔的」，與 barely noticeable 相反。

subject: english
q: The child repeated his question five times, but the guide stayed ____ and answered again without showing annoyance.
explain: patient 是「有耐心的」；重複解釋且沒有不耐煩是線索。anxious 是「焦慮的」，不是耐心等待或教導。

subject: english
q: The designer chose a ____ solution: a washable cover rather than fancy decorations that would make cleaning harder.
explain: practical 是「實用的」；捨棄華麗裝飾、選用可洗布套，重點是便利。artistic 是「藝術性的」，不合優先考慮清潔的線索。

subject: english
q: By explaining how the race raised money for charity, Ian managed to ____ his unwilling uncle to sponsor him.
explain: persuade 是「說服」；向原本不願意的叔叔說明公益目的，使他改變心意。remind 是「提醒」，不是用理由爭取同意。

subject: english
q: The paintings on display remained the artist's ____; the school had to return them when the exhibition ended.
explain: property 是「財產、所有物」；借展後須歸還，所有權仍屬藝術家。donation 是「捐贈物」，捐出後歸受贈者所有，不合暫借後歸還。

subject: english
q: The caller used a false name, but I did not believe her because I could ____ her voice.
explain: recognize 是「認出、辨識」；從聲音認出來電者，才知道她用了假名。imitate 是「模仿」，不表示認出對方。

subject: english
q: Our only radio kept losing its signal during the rescue, so we replaced it with a more ____ one.
explain: reliable 是「可靠的」；救援時收訊反覆中斷，需要運作可靠的無線電。popular 是「受歡迎的」，不能解決收訊問題。

subject: english
q: Knowing the toughest part was still ahead, the runner slowed down to ____ her strength for the final climb.
explain: reserve 是「保留」；最艱難的爬坡還在前方，因此減速保留體力。exhaust 是「耗盡」，與為最後爬坡預留體力的目的相反。

subject: english
q: Despite the seller's repeated offers of free gifts, Nora managed to ____ the temptation to buy a phone she did not need.
explain: resist 是「抵抗、忍住」；despite 表示雖有贈品仍克制購買。satisfy 是「滿足」，與抗拒不必要消費的語意相反。

subject: english
q: Because the village was so ____, delivering a single parcel required a boat trip followed by hours of walking.
explain: remote 是「偏遠的」；搭船後還要步行數小時，表示交通難以抵達。wealthy 是「富有的」，與運送路程無關。

subject: english
q: Despite winning three awards, the chef remained ____ and insisted that her assistants deserved most of the praise.
explain: modest 是「謙虛的」；得獎卻把大部分功勞歸給助手。arrogant 是「傲慢的」，與主動讚揚他人相反。

subject: english
q: A sensor will ____ the bridge's movement day and night, warning engineers whenever unusual shaking occurs.
explain: monitor 是「持續監測」；日夜觀察並在異常時警告是線索。predict 是「預測」，著重事前推估，非持續觀測現況。

subject: english
q: The shops agreed on ____ support, with each sending customers to the other so that both businesses would benefit.
explain: mutual 是「相互的」；兩店彼此介紹顧客，雙方受益。emotional 是「情緒上的」，不表示這種雙向合作。

subject: english
q: Since its owner stopped checking the brakes and changing the oil, the car has suffered from years of ____.
explain: neglect 是「疏於照顧、忽視」；不檢查煞車、不換油，指缺乏照顧。exposure 是「暴露」，此處並非強調長期受風吹雨打。

subject: english
q: Although each repair was minor, the problems were so ____ that fixing them all took the crew three full days.
explain: numerous 是「眾多的」；每項修理雖小，問題太多仍耗時三天。trivial 是「微不足道的」，不能解釋這個耗時結果。

subject: english
q: The river became an unexpected ____: its only bridge had collapsed, leaving us no way to reach the village.
explain: obstacle 是「障礙」；唯一的橋倒塌，河流阻擋了去路。landmark 是「地標」，重點在辨認位置，不是造成無法前進。

subject: english
q: The two coaches used different training methods, but the ____ was the same: both teams finished last.
explain: outcome 是「結果」；兩隊都墊底是相同的比賽結果。purpose 是「目的」，不能把失利名次當成訓練目標。

subject: english
q: The dye left a ____ mark; even after repeated washing, the dark stain remained as strong as ever.
explain: permanent 是「永久的」；反覆清洗後，深色汙漬依然不退。faint 是「淡的、不明顯的」，與顏色仍強烈的線索相反。

subject: english
q: The reporter chose a ____ printer that fitted into her bag, since she changed locations several times a day.
explain: portable 是「便於攜帶的」；經常換地點且印表機能放進包包，是攜帶需求。durable 是「耐用的」，不表示方便攜帶。

subject: english
q: By noon the flooded basement was dry, thanks to the ____ action taken as soon as the leak was reported.
explain: prompt 是「迅速的、即時的」；一接獲漏水通報就處理，是即時行動。harsh 是「嚴厲的」，不表示處理速度快。

subject: english
q: With only one ambulance, rescuers gave ____ to an unconscious patient rather than someone with a sore ankle.
explain: priority 是「優先權」；只有一輛救護車，須先處理失去意識者。permission 是「許可」，不表示救護順序。

subject: english
q: The interviewer asked about my skills, but I left out my holiday plans because they were not ____ to the job.
explain: relevant 是「相關的」，常搭配 to；求職談技能，假期計畫與職位無關。equivalent 是「等值的」，不是是否切題。

subject: english
q: Workers used old photographs to ____ the hall's original appearance, replacing modern windows with wooden ones.
explain: restore 是「恢復、修復」；依舊照換回木窗，是恢復原貌。preserve 是「保存」，用於維持已有狀態。

subject: english
q: The cafe scheduled repairs before opening to ____ disruption; doing the work at lunchtime would disturb many customers.
explain: minimize 是「使減到最少」；把維修排在開門前，可減少對午餐顧客的干擾。tolerate 是「忍受」，沒有主動減少之意。

subject: english
q: The engineer chose to ____ the design by widening its uncomfortable handle while leaving every other part unchanged.
explain: modify 是「修改、調整」；只加寬把手、其餘不變，指局部修改。replace 是「取代」，不合保留其餘設計的線索。

subject: english
q: The hotel rules made helping injured guests a staff ____, so employees could not choose whether to offer assistance.
explain: obligation 是「義務、責任」；旅館規章要求員工協助受傷旅客，不能自行決定是否協助。privilege 是「特權」，不表示必須履行的責任。

subject: english
q: In dim light, a tired driver may ____ a shadow as an animal, even when nothing is actually moving.
explain: perceive 是「察覺、視為」；光線昏暗又疲累，可能把影子看成動物。present 是「呈現、展示」，不指視覺感受。

subject: english
q: The figures are ____; several stores have yet to submit their sales reports, so the totals may change.
explain: preliminary 是「初步的」；部分報表未交，總數仍可能改變。final 是「最終的」，不合資料未齊的情況。

subject: english
q: To ____ the damaged wall before the next storm, workers added steel bars instead of just painting over the cracks.
explain: reinforce 是「加強、加固」；加鋼筋而非只遮蓋裂縫，是強化結構。inspect 是「檢查」，不包含實際補強。

subject: english
q: Ticket sales rose sharply, but higher operating costs left no profit despite the theater's increased ____.
explain: revenue 是「營收」；售票增加使營收上升，但成本吃掉利潤。expense 是「支出」，與售票所得不同。

subject: english
q: Rather than blaming bad luck, the captain gave a ____ explanation of the defeat, supported by detailed match statistics.
explain: rational 是「理性的、合乎理據的」；不用壞運氣卸責，而以比賽統計解釋。emotional 是「情緒化的」，不合數據分析。

subject: english
q: Reopening settled issues would only ____ the meeting; it would waste time without helping anyone reach a decision.
explain: prolong 是「延長」；重談已解決的事只會拖長會議，無助決策。conclude 是「結束」，與反覆討論造成的結果相反。

subject: english
q: The airline offered free meals and hotel rooms to ____ the inconvenience caused by an overnight delay.
explain: make up for 是「彌補」；提供免費餐點與住宿，是為了補償延誤造成的不便。take advantage of 是「利用」，不合補償的目的。

subject: english
q: Before the pottery class, staff moved the desks against the walls to ____ a large worktable in the middle.
explain: make room for 是「騰出空間給」；桌子靠牆移，中央才能擺大工作桌。take the place of 是「取代」，不是留出位置。

subject: english
q: With only an hour at the science museum, Ava skipped familiar displays to ____ her chance to try new experiments.
explain: make the most of 是「充分利用」；時間有限，便略過熟悉展區，把握嘗試新實驗的機會。lose sight of 是「忽略、忘記」，與主動取捨相反。

subject: english
q: The band rehearsed for weeks before all that practice began to ____: their hardest piece finally sounded smooth.
explain: pay off 是「得到回報、奏效」：數週的練習有了成效，最難的曲子才終於流暢。take shape 是「逐漸成形」，不是「有回報」；break down、fall apart 與成果相反。

subject: english
q: The email gives the new meeting time. Please ____ this information so absent members will know when to arrive.
explain: pass on 是「轉告、傳遞」；把郵件中的新時間告訴缺席成員。hold back 是「隱瞞、保留」，會使他們得不到資訊。

subject: english
q: Mason had saved for a new bicycle, but he chose to ____ a discounted one because its frame was damaged.
explain: pass up 是「放棄、錯過機會」；雖想買車且有折扣，卻因車架損壞而放棄。hold on to 是「保留」，不合尚未購買。

subject: english
q: To ____ its older buses, the company will remove a few each year as cleaner models enter service.
explain: phase out 是「逐步淘汰」；每年撤換幾輛，配合新車上路，表示分階段汰換。rule out 是「排除」，不強調逐年停止使用。

subject: english
q: The climber was in critical condition, but doctors believed she would ____ if treatment began immediately.
explain: pull through 是「度過危險、康復」；病況危急，但即時治療仍有希望。break down 是「崩潰、失常」，與醫師的樂觀判斷相反。

subject: english
q: To cover future repairs, Mei decided to ____ part of her prize money in a separate savings account.
explain: put aside 是「留存、儲蓄」；獎金存入另一帳戶，預備將來維修。use up 是「用完」，與保留備用款相反。

subject: english
q: At the planning meeting, Theo will ____ a cheaper design for discussion; the committee has not considered it yet.
explain: put forward 是「提出」；委員會尚未考慮，須先提出供討論。carry out 是「執行」，不合尚在提案階段的線索。

subject: english
q: I did not arrange to meet anyone at the festival, but I happened to ____ an old classmate near the entrance.
explain: run into 是「偶然遇見」；沒有約人卻碰到老同學，是偶遇。look after 是「照顧」，不合事先未約見面的對比。

subject: english
q: Paul had the manual beside him. Unsure how to proceed, he decided to ____ it before attempting any repairs.
explain: refer to 是「查閱、參考」。不確定如何進行維修，因此查閱身旁的手冊。look for 是「尋找」，但手冊已在身旁，不必再找。

subject: english
q: After noticing that a new student spent breaks alone, the class leader decided to ____ her and invite her to lunch.
explain: reach out to 是「主動關懷、聯繫」；發現新生落單而邀她吃飯，是主動示好。put up with 是「忍受」，不合關心的行為。

subject: english
q: Before sharing the photo, Mia checked its ____; the account that posted it had not named the photographer.
explain: source 是「來源」；貼文未註明攝影者，分享前須確認出處。subject 是「主題、拍攝對象」，無法回答照片出自何人。

subject: english
q: Repairing the machine seemed more ____ than replacing it, since only one cheap part was broken and the rest worked well.
explain: sensible 是「明智的、合理的」；機器其餘部分正常且維修便宜，只換零件很合理。ambitious 是「有雄心的」，不是花費合理。

subject: english
q: The rolls looked fine, but after several days in the cupboard they had grown ____ and were too hard to enjoy.
explain: stale 是「不新鮮的」；麵包存放多日後變硬。moist 是「濕潤的」，不能說明因放久而乾硬、難以下嚥的狀態。

subject: english
q: Alan's voice remained ____ during the interview; he sounded relaxed, spoke evenly, and never changed his volume.
explain: steady 是「平穩的」；語調放鬆、語速均勻、音量不變。tense 是「緊張的」，與放鬆的聲音表現相反。

subject: english
q: After the wash, the sleeves no longer reached my wrists; apparently, hot water had caused the sweater to ____.
explain: shrink 是「縮小、縮水」；洗後袖子短到碰不到手腕。stretch 是「拉長、伸展」，會使袖子變長，不符結果。

subject: english
q: Please leave some room at the top of the bowl, or the soup may ____ when you carry it upstairs.
explain: spill 是「灑出、溢出」；碗裝太滿，搬動時湯會灑出。spoil 是「腐壞」，不會因搬動裝滿的碗就發生。

subject: english
q: The lifeguard's ____ response left almost no time for the child to struggle before she was pulled safely from the pool.
explain: swift 是「迅速的」；孩子幾乎還來不及掙扎就獲救。gradual 是「逐漸的」，與救援迅速完成相反。

subject: english
q: Both proposals had serious drawbacks, making this a ____ decision; the committee struggled for hours before choosing.
explain: tough 在此是「困難的、棘手的」；兩案都有重大缺點，花數小時才決定。hasty 是「倉促的」，與長時間苦思不符。

subject: english
q: The novel's ____ descriptions made me feel I could see every street and smell the market food, even without pictures.
explain: vivid 是「生動鮮明的」；文字讓人彷彿看見街景、聞到食物。vague 是「模糊的」，無法帶出如此清晰的感官印象。

subject: english
q: Unable to beat rivals with speed, the team changed its ____ and began winning through careful passing and ball control.
explain: strategy 是「策略」；改以傳球與控球取勝，表示改變比賽方法。reputation 是「名聲」，不是球隊採取的戰術。

subject: english
q: Ada made a personal ____ by taking a second job for her son's tuition, giving up evenings previously spent with friends.
explain: sacrifice 是「犧牲」；為付學費而放棄與朋友相聚的晚上。promise 是「承諾」，題目強調實際付出的代價，而非口頭保證。

subject: english

Dear Museum Committee, I welcome your plan for a display about forests and climate. Tree rings would make a useful starting point. Many visitors know that counting them helps estimate a tree's age. __1__ This second story concerns the conditions in which the wood grew. It can reach back to years before local weather stations began keeping records.
In a forest where water limits growth, a dry year may leave a narrow ring. That makes the wood a possible clue to past rainfall. __2__ A tall neighbor may have blocked sunlight, or damaged roots may have slowed growth. Visitors should see why a single narrow ring leaves room for different explanations.
To strengthen the climate evidence, researchers compare trees in the same region. __3__ Such agreement points toward a shared condition rather than damage to an individual tree. A display could invite visitors to compare several records and decide whether a change affected one tree or a whole area.
Old wood can extend the record further. A dead tree may have begun growing before a living one, although both were alive during some of the same years. __4__ By matching ring patterns within that shared period, researchers can date the older wood. The combined record covers a longer period than either tree's record alone.
I hope visitors will leave asking how often the region has experienced long dry periods and how a recent drought compares. The display would show both what tree rings reveal and why careful comparison matters. Sincerely, Mei.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？

Interviewer: Why do searches for distant planets often produce records of light from stars instead of clear photographs? Astronomer: In a photograph, a faint planet can be lost beside its much brighter star. __1__ When a planet passes between us and the star, part of the star's light is hidden for a while. The star has not suddenly become smaller; something has moved across our line of sight.
Interviewer: What do you learn from two similar decreases? Astronomer: __2__ We arrange to watch the star again around that time. If its light drops as expected, the pattern supports the idea of an object following an orbit. We also compare the size and length of the decreases. Agreement among several events gives us more than a single interesting moment.
Interviewer: Does that settle the matter? Astronomer: __3__ For instance, in a pair of stars, one may regularly pass in front of the other. That also blocks light, so regular timing alone cannot identify the passing object. Further observations help researchers investigate alternatives before accepting a planet as the explanation. A promising signal begins an investigation rather than ending it.
Interviewer: Then does an unchanging record show that a star has no planets? Astronomer: __4__ Viewed from a different angle, the same orbit might produce a clear crossing. From our position, however, the planet would leave no such mark in the record. Missing a decrease in brightness is therefore not the same as finding an empty system.

Welcome to our exhibition on preparing a robot to explore another world. A strong body and reliable instruments are essential. __1__ The concern here is not an attractive appearance. Bacteria, tiny living things from Earth, could remain on the robot and travel with it. Even an explorer without a crew can have unwanted passengers.
Introducing those passengers could change an environment that scientists hope to study. There is a second difficulty, closely connected to the search for life. __2__ A chemical signal on a distant world would lose much of its value if researchers could not tell whether it came from the destination or the equipment sent there. Cleaning records can help them assess such findings.
The next section explains why cleaning is an engineering problem. Heat can reduce the number of bacteria on some parts, but high temperatures may damage sensitive equipment. __3__ A treatment that removes living things while ruining a camera would leave the mission unable to do its work. Different parts may therefore need different approaches, with tests checking the results.
The final section follows the parts after treatment. Protective covers and careful handling help prevent new material from settling on them. __4__ Otherwise, work done earlier could be undone by contact with an unclean surface. The effort has to follow the hardware through the remaining stages before launch.
As you leave, consider how much of exploration begins before departure. Protecting a future discovery involves more than choosing where a robot will look. It also involves paying attention to what the robot might take along.

Interviewer: How does your work begin? Mina: I read each chapter and consider what readers might want to find. __1__ A travel chapter might explain ways to travel cheaply without using the word budget. Someone looking under that word should still find the discussion. My headings must connect a reader's question with the author's ideas.
Interviewer: How do you decide which pages to include? Mina: One page may name a bicycle in a passing remark, while another explains how bicycles changed city travel. __2__ Otherwise, helpful pages could get lost among long lists of references. I judge what readers would learn from each page, rather than simply counting appearances of a word.
Interviewer: What happens after you have chosen the headings? Mina: __3__ For example, an entry under bikes may say "See bicycles." This link gives someone who tries the less formal name a route to the same discussion. Readers do not have to guess which term I preferred.
Interviewer: When is the job complete? Mina: Before delivery, I check every page number. __4__ If a paragraph moves during editing, a once correct number may point to the wrong place. Even a well chosen heading is useless if it sends the reader somewhere else.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: A second heading can direct readers to the main one.
I give both headings a separate list of page numbers.
A mention alone does not earn a place in the index.
For that check, I need the pages as they will be printed.
An idea can appear without the word a reader expects.

Dear Ms. Lee, Our student business has received its first large order for illustrated calendars. A local shop will buy fifty copies, paying more than our total costs for the project. We expected that order to solve our money problems. The shop, however, will pay two weeks after delivery, and the calendars have not yet been printed.
__1__ The printer requires payment before starting work, but our account cannot cover that bill. The sale should eventually leave us with more money than we spent. Until the shop pays, though, that expected gain cannot be used to get the calendars printed.
__2__ This would bring some money in before the printing bill falls due. We would need to state the delivery date clearly and explain what happens if we cannot supply the calendars. Paying early would mean the shop was trusting us before receiving anything.
__3__ We could repay a small loan from the shop payment later. But that repayment would still be due if the shop canceled its order. Unlike a buyer who pays toward calendars it expects to receive, a lender expects the borrowed money back. We must consider that difference before choosing how to fill the gap.
__4__ The printer's deadline belongs beside the date the shop promises to pay. Seeing which comes first will help us decide whether to reduce the first print run or arrange money in advance. An encouraging order is a beginning; we still have to get from the order to delivery.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: We could ask the shop to pay part of the price in advance.
I will map the two sets of dates on a payment calendar.
A profitable order can still leave us short of cash.

We could offer the shop a lower price for a larger order.

__2__ This would bring some money in before the printing bill falls due. We would need to state the delivery date clearly and explain what happens if we cannot supply the calendars. Paying early would mean the shop was trusting us before receiving anything.
__3__ We could repay a small loan from the shop payment later. But that repayment would still be due if the shop canceled its order. Unlike a buyer who pays toward calendars it expects to receive, a lender expects the borrowed money back. We must consider that difference before choosing how to fill the gap.
__4__ The printer's deadline belongs beside the date the shop promises to pay. Seeing which comes first will help us decide whether to reduce the first print run or arrange money in advance. An encouraging order is a beginning; we still have to get from the order to delivery.
q: __3__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: We could ask the shop to pay part of the price in advance.
I will map the two sets of dates on a payment calendar.
A profitable order can still leave us short of cash.
Another option is to borrow the printing money from someone outside the deal.
We could offer the shop a lower price for a larger order.
explain: borrow（借入）與後文repay（償還）相互呼應；買方取消訂單仍須還款，說明此處引入借款方案。「請店家預付」的款項來自買方，無法銜接向他人借款的責任。

subject: english
passage:
A small message above an online basket can change the way we shop: spend a little more and delivery becomes free. The message directs attention to a charge we would rather avoid. Before adding another item, however, we should examine what is happening to the whole purchase, not just to one line on the bill.
First, consider an item bought only to reach the spending target. Suppose its price is higher than the delivery charge it removes. __1__ This increase can be easy to overlook when the screen celebrates free delivery. If the item has no use to us, avoiding the fee has simply become a more expensive way to receive what we originally wanted.
__2__ If soap is already on next week's shopping list, adding it now may bring that expense forward without creating a new one. We should still consider whether we have room to store it and whether buying it elsewhere would cost less.
A third possibility is to combine an order with a friend who needs something from the same store. __3__ Someone must collect payments, divide the goods, and arrange a meeting. If one person needs an item immediately while the other can wait, a shared order may create a problem that separate purchases would avoid.
__4__ A list made before opening the website can help identify actual needs. Comparing the full amounts paid makes the money question clearer, while considering storage and coordination brings less visible costs into view. Free delivery can be useful, but the absence of a fee does not tell us the value of the whole deal.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: Buying a larger pack can lower the price of each item.
But an item we planned to buy anyway is a different case.
These cases show why the whole purchase needs a closer look.
A shared order also brings a different set of tasks.
The purchase now costs more despite the missing fee.

subject: english
passage:
At a museum, a familiar painting is sometimes missing even though its room is open. Visitors may assume that it has been sold or sent away for repair. For watercolors, however, there can be a less dramatic explanation. __1__ Staff therefore keep the lighting low in rooms containing these works, even when brighter lamps would make viewing easier.
Low lighting does not make a painting safe for unlimited display. __2__ To track this second factor, museum staff record the hours that a work spends on the wall, including quiet days when hardly anyone enters the room. After a period of display, it may return to dark storage. This prevents further exposure; it does not bring back colors already lost.
Removing a popular work creates a difficulty for visitors who came especially to see it. One response is to provide a photograph online before putting the painting away. __3__ Yet the photograph cannot offer every quality of standing before the actual painted surface. Museums should explain this difference rather than present the two experiences as equal.
The aim is to share a collection across generations, not simply to fill today's walls. A museum must consider people who will arrive years after the present exhibition closes. __4__ A notice explaining where the watercolor has gone can help visitors understand that decision. What looks like a disappointing absence may be part of responsible care.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: A damaged frame may need repairs even when the painted surface is still sound.
Even then, longer display means greater risk of fading.
Protecting the work for them can justify removing it from display today.
The light that reveals their colors can also fade them.
This keeps the image in view while the painting is stored.
explain: therefore（因此）引出降低照明，前句須說光會使水彩褪色；their colors（它們的顏色）回指水彩畫。修理畫框未交代光線的影響，不能導出調暗照明。

subject: english
passage:
Interviewer: Why are translated subtitles sometimes shorter than the speech we hear? Translator: A speaker can say a great deal while an image changes quickly. Putting every word at the bottom of the screen can force viewers into a reading race. __1__ If their eyes remain on the text, they may miss a look that explains the conversation.
Interviewer: How do you decide what to remove? Translator: Repeated greetings are sometimes less important than the information that follows them. __2__ In one scene, a character agreed to 'try' to find a room for a friend. Removing 'try' would have turned a limited offer into a promise. Shortening that line would have changed the relationship between the characters.
Interviewer: What happens when a joke depends on the original language? Translator: Words that sound alike in one language may sound quite different in another. __3__ That replacement must still suit the speaker and the situation. If the new joke introduces a fact that conflicts with the next scene, getting a laugh has come at the cost of the story.
Interviewer: How do you check the finished version? Translator: I watch it at normal speed with people who have not read the script. __4__ If they spend a serious scene struggling to finish a line, I revise it. If they misunderstand an important offer, I restore the missing meaning. A successful subtitle supports the film while asking for as little attention as possible.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: A new joke may be needed to create a similar effect.
The trial tests both reading speed and understanding.
A longer line is therefore a more accurate translation.
Yet a short word can matter more than a long phrase.
That race leaves little time to watch the action.
explain: That race（那場搶讀）回指前句的 reading race，說明搶讀會排擠觀看畫面的時間，後句以漏看表情具體化。「較長字幕較準確」未承接這項後果。

subject: english
passage:
Dear Iris, I spent Friday with a family in Sweden during Midsummer, a celebration held in June. When we arrived at the village green, a long pole lay on the grass beside piles of leaves and flowers. Several neighbors were still tying plants to its wooden frame. __1__ By the time it stood upright, even my awkward contributions had become part of the display.
Once the music started, people formed a circle around the decorated pole. I remained at the edge, expecting to watch skilled local dancers. Then my host took my hand. __2__ She repeated the movements slowly, and I copied the people beside me. The children made mistakes too, but nobody seemed concerned about producing a perfect performance for visitors.
Later, we shared potatoes and strawberries at a long outdoor table. I went inside to fetch a jacket. __3__ It was already late in the evening, although the garden still looked bright. The long daylight around late June had confused my usual sense of an evening's progress. Outside, no one seemed in a hurry to end the conversation.
Before the visit, I had wondered what the celebration offered to people who disliked dancing. __4__ A quiet neighbor who had stayed outside the circle now passed dishes around and told me about the village. His part in the occasion was different from my host's, but just as welcoming. My photographs show flowers and dancers; they cannot fully show the conversations that made me feel at home. Love, Nina.
q: __1__ 處最適合填入哪一個句子？
choices: The circle had room for learners as well as experts.
Sharing the meal gave them a different way to join in.
They asked me to help before we lifted it into place.
The kitchen clock told a different story from the garden.
We had waited for darkness before the dancing began.
explain: They 指鄰居，it 指仍平躺的柱子；lift（抬起）銜接後句直立，也解釋作者如何參與。「舞圈容得下初學者」會提早跳到尚未開始的跳舞活動。
